rounds.rationale: Select these 15 roles to cover the supplied compiler evidence, descriptor mappings, timed conversions, memory layouts, and correctness. assembly_audit and compiler_codegen examine the supplied machine code against its source hashes. n512_fast_path reviews the unmeasured TA and TT wrappers: TA requires transpose(B) and original A; TT requires both physical transposes. The exact TB wrapper has now failed promotion on AC and battery; its results do not measure TA or TT or isolate component costs. a_transpose, panel_packing, b_panel_layout, and transpose_fusion cover distinct conversion and packing designs. cache_blocking, loop_order, and cache_conflict_layout cover traversal and storage hypotheses without assuming a cache cause. vector_access and sme_fp32_tiles cover operand access and the four available ZA.S tiles; the existing ZA0/ZA1-before-ZA2/ZA3 stores are not new. scratch_lifetime and streaming_region_cost cover timed temporary storage and valid SME boundaries. tail_alignment checks bounds and general-size correctness. Omit dedicated counter, pointer, prefetch, and K-schedule roles this round because many prior variants already exist. Each advisor must identify a distinct source change or abstain. This roster selects no experiment; joint board ranking remains required. Advice remains unverified. Preserve all fixed constraints, ten alternating candidate/control pairs, best-of-three reports, the 5% separated-ranges gate, and held-out validation. Report historical and fresh same-mode comparisons separately.

board.recommendation: Propose a four-step K-loop unroll in both full512 compute loops. Repeat the existing paired LD1W, pointer advances, and four FMOPA operations four times in order, then decrement the counter by four and branch. Keep each ZA tile’s FP32 accumulation order and total of 512 K steps unchanged; retain a cleanup path if the loop must support other counts. In the supplied instructions, each K step includes two loads, two pointer updates, four FMOPAs, and loop control. The hypothesis is that fewer loop-control instructions per K step may help. This is unverified advice, not a measured effect. Check full512 correctness and fresh inputs, general sizes and tails, n<=0, full output overwrite, ABI, tolerance 0.002, allocation-failure fallback, and license notices. Then use ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with unchanged settings; preserve best-of-three timing and apply the existing promotion and held-out gates.
board.risks: This extends the previously tested two-step unroll and may increase code size or instruction scheduling pressure. The supplied history does not establish that loop control limits throughput, and instruction count alone does not predict timing. Preserve the fixed FP32 arithmetic and all 512 ordered updates; do not attribute any joint score change to this proposal alone.

This keeps all allocation and packing inside `gemm` and changes the measured 128 KiB scratch lifetime and traversal together. board.recommendation: Propose a fused 16×16 A-tile transpose and compute path for n=512. Load the row-major tile into SVE vectors, transpose it with vector zip/unzip operations, then feed its 16 column vectors and the matching B values to the existing FP32 MOPA accumulator. Keep the output accumulator in ZA across all 512 K values; do not use ZA for the input transpose. Write C with the existing stores. The hypothesis is that removing full A-stack packing and its later reads may offset the repeated small-tile transpose work. This is unverified. There are 16 column panels, so this recomputes the transpose of every A element 16 times: 4,194,304 FP32 elements (16 MiB read and 16 MiB of transposed values produced) versus one full A pass of 262,144 elements (1 MiB) in the existing packing path. Count all tile loads, vector shuffles, allocation, and stores in the timed call.

SVE transpose shuffles and register pressure may also slow the MOPA loop or require spills; spills could erase the expected benefit. Preserve each output's K accumulation order and FP32 arithmetic. Validate fresh inputs against the frozen tolerance, full C overwrite, n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0, and allocation-failure behavior. Do not infer an isolated transpose cost or causal benefit from whole-call scores.
